Title: LLMs as Assistants for Divergent Thinking in Software Architecture Design  
Claim: LLMs can effectively support architects in generating a wide range of design alternatives and evaluating their pros and cons, but they are not well suited for the convergent, integrative phase of design.  
Evidence: "While LLMs may not excel at the latter, they can be extremely useful in the former. LLMs can aid an architect in “scanning the horizon” for possible solutions and quickly enumerating their well-known pros and cons. / This can make the search for appropriate design concepts much more thorough: the LLM may have access to far more relevant data about design concepts than your average architect, and more efficient: the LLM, by enumerating pros and cons, can quickly help an architect eliminate large numbers of alternatives."  
Labels: Divergent thinking, Convergent thinking, LLM limitations, Design assistance  
Conditions: Based on authors' workshop experience and observations of LLM behavior.  
Limits: Findings derived from limited design problems; generalization to complex real-world scenarios remains untested.

Title: Research Priorities for AI in Software Architecture: Transparency, Accountability, and Explainability  
Claim: Workshop participants identified transparency and accountability as the foremost concerns for AI in software architecture, with additional priorities including explainability, handling of software artifacts, and quality attributes such as maintainability and security.  
Evidence: "Transparency and accountability emerged as the top concerns across groups. Group 3 reiterated the need for explainability. / Group 4 added that quality attributes, such as maintainability, security, and ethical considerations should be central to future AI systems in this domain."  
Labels: AI ethics, Transparency, Accountability, Explainability, Quality attributes, Research priorities  
Conditions: Derived from participants in a workshop setting.  
Limits: The priorities may differ in other contexts; the list is not exhaustive.
